claim: CRM1 binds highly variable nuclear export signals (NESs) in hundreds of different cargoes.
source: Nuclear export receptor CRM1 binds highly variable nuclear export signals (NESs) in hundreds of different cargoes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Fornerod et al., 1997; Fukuda et al., 1997; Stade et al., 1997; Ossareh-Nazari et al., 1997; Xu et al., 2012a; Kırlı et al., 2015; Thakar et al., 2013).

claim: CRM1 binds NESs in both polypeptide orientations.
source: Previously we have shown that CRM1 binds NESs in both polypeptide orientations (Fung et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors (Fung et al., 2015).

claim: Crystal structures of CRM1 bound to eight additional NESs reveal diverse conformations that range from loop-like to all-helix.
source: Here, we show crystal structures of CRM1 bound to eight additional NESs which reveal diverse conformations that range from loop-like to all-helix, which occupy different extents of the invariant NES-binding groove.
evidence: This is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript, including Figures 1 and 2 showing the different NES structures.

claim: Analysis of all NES structures show 5-6 distinct backbone conformations.
source: Analysis of all NES structures show 5-6 distinct backbone conformations where the only conserved secondary structural element is one turn of helix that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis presented in Figure 3A showing the overlay of different NES structures.

claim: The only conserved secondary structural element in NESs is one turn of helix that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove.
source: Analysis of all NES structures show 5-6 distinct backbone conformations where the only conserved secondary structural element is one turn of helix that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3A with a grey rectangle highlighting the conserved helix turn.

claim: All NESs participate in main chain hydrogen bonding with human CRM1 Lys568 side chain.
source: All NESs also participate in main chain hydrogen bonding with human CRM1 Lys568 side chain, which acts as a specificity filter that prevents binding of non-NES peptides.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing hydrogen bonds in Figures 1, 2, and 3, and by mutagenesis data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Human CRM1 Lys568 acts as a specificity filter that prevents binding of non-NES peptides.
source: All NESs also participate in main chain hydrogen bonding with human CRM1 Lys568 side chain, which acts as a specificity filter that prevents binding of non-NES peptides.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis experiments showing that K568A and K568M mutants bind false positive NES sequences (Figure 4A), and by structural data showing steric clashes (Figure 4B,C).

claim: The large conformational range of NES backbones explains the lack of a fixed pattern for its 3-5 hydrophobic anchor residues.
source: The large conformational range of NES backbones explains the lack of a fixed pattern for its 3-5 hydrophobic anchor residues, which in turn explains the large array of peptide sequences that can function as NESs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural data showing diverse NES conformations (Figures 1-3).

claim: NES sequences are very diverse but each usually has 4–5 hydrophobic residues (often Leu/Val/Ile/Phe/Met; labeled Ф0–5).
source: NES sequences are very diverse but each usually has 4–5 hydrophobic residues (often Leu/Val/Ile/Phe/Met; labeled Ф0–5) that bind hydrophobic pockets (labeled P0–P4) in a hydrophobic groove formed by HEAT repeats 11 and 12 of CRM1 (9–16).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NES hydrophobic anchor residues bind hydrophobic pockets (labeled P0–P4) in a hydrophobic groove formed by HEAT repeats 11 and 12 of CRM1.
source: NES sequences are very diverse but each usually has 4–5 hydrophobic residues (often Leu/Val/Ile/Phe/Met; labeled Ф0–5) that bind hydrophobic pockets (labeled P0–P4) in a hydrophobic groove formed by HEAT repeats 11 and 12 of CRM1 (9–16).
evidence: This is supported by citations and by structural data showing the binding pockets in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The hydrophobic anchor residues are arranged in many ways, currently described by ten consensus patterns for corresponding NES classes 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 2, 3, 1a-R, 1b-R, 1c-R and 1d-R.
source: The hydrophobic anchor residues are arranged in many ways, currently described by ten consensus patterns for corresponding NES classes 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 2, 3, 1a-R, 1b-R, 1c-R and 1d-R (Figure 1A) (Fung et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Fung et al., 2015) and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Previous structures of CRM1 bound to five different NESs showed virtually identical NES-binding grooves.
source: Previous structures of CRM1 bound to five different NESs showed virtually identical NES-binding grooves (Fung et al., 2015; Monecke et al., 2009; Dong et al., 2009; Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: NESs from Snurportin-1 (SNUPNNES; class 1c) and Protein Kinase A Inhibitor (PKINES; class 1a) bind CRM1 as α-helix followed by a short β-strand.
source: NESs from Snurportin-1 (SNUPNNES; class 1c) and Protein Kinase A Inhibitor (PKINES; class 1a) bind CRM1 as α-helix followed by a short β-strand, while the proline-rich NES from HIV-1 REV (RevNES; class 2) adopts mostly extended conformation (Figure 1B) (Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Güttler et al., 2010) and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The proline-rich NES from HIV-1 REV (RevNES; class 2) adopts mostly extended conformation.
source: NESs from Snurportin-1 (SNUPNNES; class 1c) and Protein Kinase A Inhibitor (PKINES; class 1a) bind CRM1 as α-helix followed by a short β-strand, while the proline-rich NES from HIV-1 REV (RevNES; class 2) adopts mostly extended conformation (Figure 1B) (Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Güttler et al., 2010) and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The majority of CRM1-NES interactions involve NES hydrophobic anchor side chains, with very few polar and main chain interactions.
source: The majority of CRM1-NES interactions involve NES hydrophobic anchor side chains, with very few polar and main chain interactions.
evidence: This is based on analysis of previous structures cited (Güttler et al., 2010).

claim: NESs from kinase RIO2 and cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding protein 4 (hRio2NES, CPEB4NES) do not adopt all-helical conformations but unexpectedly adopt helix-strand conformations that bind CRM1 in the opposite or minus (−) polypeptide direction.
source: Structures of such NESs from kinase RIO2 and cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding protein 4 (hRio2NES, CPEB4NES) showed that they do not adopt all-helical conformations but unexpectedly adopt helix-strand conformations that bind CRM1 in the opposite or minus (−) polypeptide direction to that of SNUPNNES, PKINES and RevNES ((+) NESs) (Fung et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Fung et al., 2015).

claim: hRio2NES and CPEB4NES were reclassified as class 1a-R NESs.
source: hRio2NES and CPEB4NES were hence reclassified as class 1a-R NESs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Eight NESs bind HsCRM1 in the presence of RanGTP with dissociation constants (KDs) of 670 nM-20 μM.
source: All eight NESs bind HsCRM1 in the presence of RanGTP with dissociation constants (KDs) of 670 nM-20 μM, and were crystallized bound to the previously described engineered ScCRM1-RanGppNHp-Yrb1p complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—source data 1, 2 and 3) (Fung et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by binding data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: NES-bound CRM1 grooves in the structures (2.1–2.4 Å resolution) resemble the PKINES-bound MmCRM1 groove (Cα/all-atom rmsds 0.5 Å/1.1 Å for 85 groove residues).
source: NES-bound CRM1 grooves in the structures (2.1–2.4 Å resolution) resemble the PKINES-bound MmCRM1 groove (Cα/all-atom rmsds 0.5 Å/1.1 Å for 85 groove residues), and all NESs use 4–5 hydrophobic anchor residues to bind P0-P4 hydrophobic pockets of CRM1 (Figures 1D–F and 2) (Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison data and shown in Figures 1D-F and 2.

claim: All NESs use 4–5 hydrophobic anchor residues to bind P0-P4 hydrophobic pockets of CRM1.
source: NES-bound CRM1 grooves in the structures (2.1–2.4 Å resolution) resemble the PKINES-bound MmCRM1 groove (Cα/all-atom rmsds 0.5 Å/1.1 Å for 85 groove residues), and all NESs use 4–5 hydrophobic anchor residues to bind P0-P4 hydrophobic pockets of CRM1 (Figures 1D–F and 2) (Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figures 1D-F and 2.

claim: Class 3 NESs from mouse diaphanous homolog 3 (mDia2NES) and the cell division cycle 7-related protein kinase (CDC7NES) are all-helix peptides, both forming 3-turn α-helices.
source: Class 3 NESs from mouse diaphanous homolog 3 (mDia2NES: 1179SVPEVEALLARLRAL1193) and the cell division cycle 7-related protein kinase (CDC7NES: 456QDLRKLCERLRGMDSSTP473) are indeed all-helix peptides, both forming 3-turn α-helices that occupy only the wide part of the CRM1 groove (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: mDia2NES and CDC7NES occupy only the wide part of the CRM1 groove.
source: Class 3 NESs from mouse diaphanous homolog 3 (mDia2NES: 1179SVPEVEALLARLRAL1193) and the cell division cycle 7-related protein kinase (CDC7NES: 456QDLRKLCERLRGMDSSTP473) are indeed all-helix peptides, both forming 3-turn α-helices that occupy only the wide part of the CRM1 groove (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The last residue of the mDia2 protein (Leu1193) binds the CRM1 P3 pocket leaving the P4 pocket empty.
source: The last residue of the mDia2 protein (Leu1193) binds the CRM1 P3 pocket leaving the P4 pocket empty.
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CDC7NES exits the groove after Met468 or Φ3.
source: CDC7NES is far from the protein C-terminus but structures of longer peptides suggest that CDC7NESexits the groove after Met468 or Φ3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The mDia2NES and CDC7NES sequence patterns should be Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3.
source: The mDia2NES and CDC7NESsequence patterns should thus be Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing that P4 pocket is not occupied.

claim: The Φ4 anchor position is not used in mDia2NES and CDC7NES even though Φ4 is key for activities of several other NESs.
source: The Φ4 anchor position is clearly not used in mDia2NES and CDC7NES even though Φ4 is key for activities of several other NESs (Wen et al., 1995; Meyer et al., 1996; Richards et al., 1996; Scott et al., 2002; Tsukahara and Maru, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by structural data and citations to previous work showing importance of Φ4 in other NESs.

claim: The number of Φ anchor residues necessary for CRM1 binding can vary between 3–5.
source: The number of Φ anchor residues necessary for CRM1 binding can vary between 3–5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: X11L2NES (55SSLQELVQQFEALPGDLV72) forms a 3-turn α-helix from residues 57LQELVQQFEAL67 and a type I β-turn from residues 68PGDL71.
source: A third class 3-matching NES from beta-amyloid binding protein X11L2 (X11L2NES: 55SSLQELVQQFEALPGDLV72) binds differently (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4). 57LQELVQQFEAL67 forms a 3-turn α-helix, 68PGDL71 forms a type I β-turn, and X11L2NES therefore exhibits a new Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3XXXΦ4 (class 4) pattern.
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: X11L2NES exhibits a new Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3XXXΦ4 (class 4) pattern.
source: A third class 3-matching NES from beta-amyloid binding protein X11L2 (X11L2NES: 55SSLQELVQQFEALPGDLV72) binds differently (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4). 57LQELVQQFEAL67 forms a 3-turn α-helix, 68PGDL71 forms a type I β-turn, and X11L2NES therefore exhibits a new Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3XXXΦ4 (class 4) pattern.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing the helix-β-turn conformation.

claim: The previous structure of RevNES (class 2) suggested that its three prolines may constrain against a helical conformation.
source: The previous structure of RevNES (class 2) suggested that its three prolines may constrain against a helical conformation (Figure 1B) (Güttler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Güttler et al., 2010) and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Class 2 NESs in SMAD4NES and FMRPNES have few to no prolines but still bind CRM1 with mostly loop-like structures.
source: Class 2 NESs in the Mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 4 protein (SMAD4NES: 133YERVVSPGIDLSGLTLQ149) and the fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRPNES: 423YLKEVDQLRLERLQI437) have few to no prolines but still bind CRM1 with mostly loop-like structures (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: HDAC5NES and PaxNES have NESs with non-α-helical class 1b pattern (Ф1XXФ2XXФ3XФ4), but the peptides bind according to the class 1a pattern instead.
source: Histone deacetylase 5 (HDAC5NES: 1082EAETVSAMALLSVG1095) and Paxillin (PaxNES: 264RELDELMASLSDFKFMAQ281) have NESs with non-α-helical class 1b pattern (Ф1XXФ2XXФ3XФ4), but the peptides bind according to the class 1a pattern instead (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is no other experimentally verified NES in the databases that unambiguously match class 1b pattern.
source: This left no other experimentally verified NES in the databases that unambiguously match class 1b pattern (Kosugi et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2012c).
evidence: This is based on analysis of NES databases cited (Kosugi et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2012c).

claim: FMRP-1bNES forms a short 1.5-turn 310 helix followed by a 3-residue β-strand.
source: We engineered a class 1b NES by adding an alanine to FMRPNES (FMRP-1bNES; YLKEVDQLRALERLQID), which forms a short 1.5-turn 310 helix followed by a 3-residue β-strand (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: The 310 helix favorably presents Φ1 and Φ2 into the CRM1 groove.
source: The 310 helix favorably presents Φ1 and Φ2 into the CRM1 groove and natural class 1b NESs are likely to bind similarly.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data of FMRP-1bNES.

claim: Natural class 1b NESs are likely to bind similarly to FMRP-1bNES.
source: The 310 helix favorably presents Φ1 and Φ2 into the CRM1 groove and natural class 1b NESs are likely to bind similarly.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural data of the engineered FMRP-1bNES.

claim: Structures of >13 different CRM1-bound NESs may be sorted into five or six groups according to peptide backbone conformations.
source: Structures of >13 different CRM1-bound NESs are now available, and may be sorted into five or six groups according to peptide backbone conformations (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Class 1 NESs are helix-strand peptides with either α-helices (class 1a, 1c) or 310 helices (class 1b).
source: Class 1 NESs are helix-strand peptides with either α-helices (class 1a, 1c) or 310 helices (class 1b).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of multiple NES structures.

claim: Class 1-R NESs are strand-helix peptides.
source: Class 1-R NESs are strand-helix peptides, class 2 NESs are mostly loop-like and class 3 NESs are all-helix peptides.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of multiple NES structures.

claim: Class 2 NESs are mostly loop-like.
source: Class 1-R NESs are strand-helix peptides, class 2 NESs are mostly loop-like and class 3 NESs are all-helix peptides.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of multiple NES structures.

claim: Class 3 NESs are all-helix peptides.
source: Class 1-R NESs are strand-helix peptides, class 2 NESs are mostly loop-like and class 3 NESs are all-helix peptides.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of multiple NES structures.

claim: The helix-β-turn X11L2NES structure revealed a new Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3XXXΦ4 (class 4) pattern.
source: The helix-β-turn X11L2NES structure revealed a new Φ0XXΦ1XXXΦ2XXΦ3XXXΦ4 (class 4) pattern.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of X11L2NES shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In all (+) NESs, main chain carbonyls of Φ2+1 and Φ3 residues in the 1-turn helix element hydrogen bonds with the ScCRM1 Lys579 (or MmCRM1/HsCRM1 Lys568) side chain.
source: In all (+) NESs, main chain carbonyls of Φ2+1 and Φ3 residues in the 1-turn helix element hydrogen bonds with the ScCRM1 Lys579 (or MmCRM1/HsCRM1 Lys568) side chain, much like niche3/4 motifs where carbonyls of residues i and i + 2 or i + 3 coordinate a cationic group (Torrance et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Torrance et al., 2009.

claim: The Φ3-Lys579 hydrogen bond is possible only because the β-strand psi angle turns Φ3 carbonyl towards Lys579.
source: The Φ3-Lys579 hydrogen bond is possible only because the β-strand psi angle turns Φ3 carbonyl towards Lys579 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: NES helix-Lys579 hydrogen bonds are absent in (−) NESs as backbone carbonyls point in the opposite direction.
source: NES helix-Lys579 hydrogen bonds are absent in (−) NESs as backbone carbonyls point in the opposite direction.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data of (−) NESs shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In (−) NESs, carbonyls of the N-terminal β-strand hydrogen bond with Lys579.
source: Here, carbonyls of the N-terminal β-strand hydrogen bond with Lys579 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Another common structural feature of NESs is hydrogen bonding between NES backbone and ScCRM1 Lys579 (HsCRM1 Lys568).
source: Therefore, another common structural feature of NESs is hydrogen bonding between NES backbone and ScCRM1 Lys579 (HsCRM1 Lys568).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing hydrogen bonds in both (+) and (−) NESs.

claim: Mutations of HsCRM1 Lys568 impair NES binding.
source: Mutations of HsCRM1 Lys568 impair NES binding.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutants HsCRM1(K568A) and HsCRM1(K568M) bind FITC-PKINES two to three orders of magnitude weaker than wild type HsCRM1.
source: Mutants HsCRM1(K568A) and HsCRM1(K568M) bind FITC-PKINES two to three orders of magnitude weaker than wild type HsCRM1, supporting the importance of Lys568-NES interactions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by binding data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: An active NES can use many different backbone conformations to present 3–5 hydrophobic anchor residues into 3–5 CRM1 hydrophobic pockets.
source: In summary, an active NES (1) can use many different backbone conformations to present 3–5 hydrophobic anchor residues into 3–5 CRM1 hydrophobic pockets (P0 and/or P4 are sometimes not used), (2) has one turn of helix with helix-strand transition that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove and (3) has backbone conformation that can hydrogen bond with Lys568 of HsCRM1.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the structural data presented.

claim: P0 and/or P4 pockets are sometimes not used by NESs.
source: In summary, an active NES (1) can use many different backbone conformations to present 3–5 hydrophobic anchor residues into 3–5 CRM1 hydrophobic pockets (P0 and/or P4 are sometimes not used), (2) has one turn of helix with helix-strand transition that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove and (3) has backbone conformation that can hydrogen bond with Lys568 of HsCRM1.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing mDia2NES and CDC7NES not using P4 pocket.

claim: An active NES has one turn of helix with helix-strand transition that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove.
source: In summary, an active NES (1) can use many different backbone conformations to present 3–5 hydrophobic anchor residues into 3–5 CRM1 hydrophobic pockets (P0 and/or P4 are sometimes not used), (2) has one turn of helix with helix-strand transition that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove and (3) has backbone conformation that can hydrogen bond with Lys568 of HsCRM1.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the structural data presented.

claim: An active NES has backbone conformation that can hydrogen bond with Lys568 of HsCRM1.
source: In summary, an active NES (1) can use many different backbone conformations to present 3–5 hydrophobic anchor residues into 3–5 CRM1 hydrophobic pockets (P0 and/or P4 are sometimes not used), (2) has one turn of helix with helix-strand transition that binds the central portion of the CRM1 groove and (3) has backbone conformation that can hydrogen bond with Lys568 of HsCRM1.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the structural data presented.

claim: Arrangement of hydrophobic pockets in the groove likely selects NESs with suitably placed Φ residues.
source: Arrangement of hydrophobic pockets in the groove likely selects NESs with suitably placed Φ residues.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural data.

claim: Groove shape, tapering and most constricted at ScCRM1 Lys579 (HsCRM1 Lys568), likely selects for NES helices that transition to strands or NES helices that end.
source: Groove shape, tapering and most constricted at ScCRM1 Lys579 (HsCRM1 Lys568), likely selects for NES helices that transition to strands or NES helices that end (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Wild type HsCRM1 does not bind Hxk2pep, DEAF1pep, and COMMD1pep peptides.
source: Wild type HsCRM1 does not bind the peptides but HsCRM1(K568A) binds Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep, and HsCRM1(K568M) binds DEAF1pep but not Hxk2pep, suggesting that Lys568 is important in filtering out false positive NESs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HsCRM1(K568A) binds Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep.
source: Wild type HsCRM1 does not bind the peptides but HsCRM1(K568A) binds Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep, and HsCRM1(K568M) binds DEAF1pep but not Hxk2pep, suggesting that Lys568 is important in filtering out false positive NESs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HsCRM1(K568M) binds DEAF1pep but not Hxk2pep.
source: Wild type HsCRM1 does not bind the peptides but HsCRM1(K568A) binds Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep, and HsCRM1(K568M) binds DEAF1pep but not Hxk2pep, suggesting that Lys568 is important in filtering out false positive NESs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lys568 is important in filtering out false positive NESs.
source: Wild type HsCRM1 does not bind the peptides but HsCRM1(K568A) binds Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep, and HsCRM1(K568M) binds DEAF1pep but not Hxk2pep, suggesting that Lys568 is important in filtering out false positive NESs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis data showing differential binding of false positive NESs to mutant CRM1.

claim: Both ScCRM1(K579A)-bound Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep are all-helix peptides.
source: Both ScCRM1(K579A)-bound Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep are all-helix peptides (Figure 4B,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 4B,C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fourth turn of the Hxk2pep helix packs into hydrophobic space widened by removal and rearrangement of the Lys579 and Glu582 side chains, respectively.
source: The fourth turn of the Hxk2pep helix packs into hydrophobic space widened by removal and rearrangement of the Lys579 and Glu582 side chains, respectively (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The 2.5-turn α-helix of DEAF1pep binds in the (−) direction and is slightly longer than helices in true (−) NESs.
source: The 2.5-turn α-helix of DEAF1pepbinds in the (−) direction and is slightly longer than helices in true (−) NESs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Superpositions of Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep onto wild type CRM1 grooves show the fourth turn of the Hxk2pep helix and the N-terminus of the DEAF1pep helix clashing with ScCRM1 Lys579/MmCRM1 Lys568 side chains.
source: Superpositions of Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep onto wild type CRM1 grooves show the fourth turn of the Hxk2pep helix and the N-terminus of the DEAF1pep helix clashing with ScCRM1 Lys579/MmCRM1 Lys568 side chains (Figure 4B,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural superposition data shown in Figure 4B,C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The rest of the mutant ScCRM1(K579A) groove is highly similar to the wild type groove.
source: The rest of the mutant ScCRM1(K579A) groove is highly similar to the wild type groove.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of mutant and wild type CRM1 grooves.

claim: The key feature of the wild type groove that prevents Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep binding is Lys568.
source: Therefore, the key feature of the wild type groove that prevents Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep binding is Lys568, which is not only a critical hydrogen bond donor for binding NESs, but its long side chain also blocks binding of sequences that do not meet NES structural requirements.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and mutagenesis data.

claim: Lys568 is not only a critical hydrogen bond donor for binding NESs, but its long side chain also blocks binding of sequences that do not meet NES structural requirements.
source: Therefore, the key feature of the wild type groove that prevents Hxk2pep and DEAF1pep binding is Lys568, which is not only a critical hydrogen bond donor for binding NESs, but its long side chain also blocks binding of sequences that do not meet NES structural requirements.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and mutagenesis data showing both hydrogen bonding and steric blocking functions.

claim: Class 1a, 1b, 1c, 2, 3, 4 and 1a-R NES structures show 5–6 distinct backbone conformations that match their respective hydrophobic sequence patterns.
source: Class 1a, 1b, 1c, 2, 3, 4 and 1a-R NES structures show 5–6 distinct backbone conformations that match their respective hydrophobic sequence patterns.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural data presented.

claim: Class 1d NESs (Ф1XXФ2XXXФ3XФ4) are likely α-helix-strand.
source: We can infer structures of remaining NES classes: class 1d NESs (Ф1XXФ2XXXФ3XФ4) are likely α-helix-strand and other (−) NES classes are likely the reverse of their (+) counterparts.
evidence: This is speculation based on the patterns observed in other NES classes.

claim: Other (−) NES classes are likely the reverse of their (+) counterparts.
